# tests/fixtures/reference-digests.txt -- TE-62/TE-78/TE-82 (U0 slice B):
# a NAMED TABLE, one line per named quantity per (artifact, corpus),
# computed by the SHIPPED encoder's own timed call, in the same process,
# at whole-document chunk budget -- never a value any seat fabricates or
# transcribes from the fold-4 probe's own reference-digests.txt (which
# was measured against a DIFFERENT engine pin, v1.2.0, and PS-1's
# pre-fold-11 seam shape -- read as an anchor's SHAPE and provenance
# discipline, never copied as a value: `Claude/Plans/SuperEmbedder_Plan.md`
# sec 3.3's own producer-identity rule forbids a field computed from a
# description of an input, which a transcribed digest would be here).
#
# TE-82 RULING (D-SLM6072/D-SLM6073/D-SLM6094, and the open question
# TE-80's own record filed): C39 (`tests/c39_seam_digest_test.cpp`) and
# the witness matrix (`tests/witness_structural_matrix.py`) grade two
# DIFFERENT quantities against this ONE fixture, and TE-78 had recomposed
# the single prior anchor line to hold only one of them (`witness_sha`),
# which is why C39 read a mismatch it was correct to report (TE-76 review
# F-1; TE-80's own filed finding). Both values now live here, each under
# its own name -- C39's scope is unchanged (it still computes and compares
# ONLY W-B's own seam digest, exactly what sec 8's C39 row and this file's
# header have always specified); the witness's composition is unchanged
# (sec 4.4b's `witness_sha = SHA-256(W-A || W-B || W-Q)`). "A leg whose
# anchor does not reproduce the committed reference is measuring a
# different encoder, engine pin, artifact or corpus" (sec 4.4b) now holds
# for both rows independently.
#
# FORMAT: "<name> <sha256-hex>", one entry per line, lowercase hex.
# TE-83 (TE-81 review N-4): `tests/c39_seam_digest_test.cpp`'s own
# `ReadAnchorByName()` parses and matches the NAME on every non-comment
# line -- row order is not significant, and this table can gain rows
# above or below either of these two without affecting either reader
# (verified at source, TE-83). `witness_sha` is not parsed
# programmatically by anything under `tests/` today
# (`tests/witness_structural_matrix.py`'s own C31(v)/C36(b) legs run
# `semb_witness` directly and compare its freshly-computed value against
# ITSELF across a mutant build, never against this file) -- it is
# committed here as the project's one pinned reference value for the
# composed fingerprint, for a human reader or a future cell to compare
# against.
#
# c39_seam_digest: SHA-256 over `semb_seam_serialize_document`'s own
# output bytes (W-B alone) for the document below, through the engine's
# portable `superslm::Sha256Hash`. Recomputed at the v1.5.0 pin from the
# BUILT c39_seam_digest_test's own code path (never re-derived by hand):
# two independent process invocations under each of MSVC 19.33 and
# clang-cl 18.1.8 produced this exact digest, byte for byte. The anchor
# moves whenever the engine pin moves the regenerated artifact's bytes or
# the forward, which the v1.5.0 pin does.
#
# witness_sha: SHA-256(W-A digest || W-B digest || W-Q placeholder
# digest), sec 4.4b's own composed fingerprint. Recomputed at v1.5.0 via
# `semb_witness --model build/_scratch/synthetic_te62_c39.sslm --tokens
# 3,17,42,5,90 --chunk-budget 0` (two processes under each compiler), and
# reproduced by both independent baselines of the pin-bump construction
# (`tools/engine_side_wa_perturbation.py`), whose C36(a) and C38 readings
# all held.
#
# Both rows: the document is `tests/c39_seam_digest_test.cpp`'s own
# committed 5-token document (kTokenIds = {3, 17, 42, 5, 90}) at
# chunk_budget=0 (one whole-document call), against the regenerated
# synthetic artifact `build/_scratch/synthetic_te62_c39.sslm` (pinned tag
# v1.5.0, `tests/fixtures/regenerate_synthetic_artifact.py`'s own output).
# Artifact fingerprint (SHA-256 of that .sslm file's own bytes,
